logic.note: The I2S stream is received as whole blocks of samples with their sample rate, bit depth and channel count (whatever the board's I2S peripheral sent); BCLK / LRC edges, clock jitter and frame-sync errors are not simulated.

timing.note: Blocks arrive at the virtual time the board's DMA moved them, not sample by sample.

analog.note: Output is the block's RMS level × gain as an RMS voltage across OUT+ / OUT- (solved as DC into the speaker's coil resistance). No filtering, distortion, clipping shape or click/pop suppression.

power.note: Supply current follows output power at ~85 % efficiency plus 2.4 mA quiescent.

emulates: Whether the board sends I2S audio and how loud it is
Channel select and shutdown from the SD pin

The sound itself on the page that follows faber serve: each run's I2S stream is kept as a WAV and played with WebAudio in step with the run (mono, 16 kHz; never under a test driver; the speaker's frequency response is not applied)
doesNotEmulate: The waveform on the speaker (frequency response, distortion)
I2S clock or format mismatches (a wrong bit depth on real hardware sounds like noise)
testOnRealDevice: Listen for hiss and pops at start-up; keep the speaker wires short
Check the I2S format (Philips, 16 or 32 bit) matches what the library sends
Never wire OUT- to GND: the output is bridge-tied
Loudness: a full-scale signal at 5 V can push more watts than a small speaker takes (check_design says how far to scale the samples)
